subject.title: fix(imessage): repair DM sender fallback before pairing

question: Should this iMessage identity repair land as a narrow sender rewrite only, or should unrepairable local-sender direct payloads fail closed before access control?
rationale: The repaired sender becomes the authorization subject and delivery target, so the permanent behavior is an identity-boundary decision rather than only a local refactor.

options.title: Fix Normalization And Require Live Proof
options.body: Update peer selection to use canonical iMessage handle normalization, keep or add focused regression coverage, and require redacted after-fix proof showing pairing or replies target the peer chat.

options.title: Accept Source-Only Identity Risk
options.body: Maintainers could merge based on source review plus pre-fix incident evidence while owning the remaining live-payload and candidate-selection uncertainty.

options.title: Pause Until The Remaining Failure Is Clear
options.body: If the author's current failure is a different root cause, pause this branch and track the narrower remaining iMessage issue separately.

recommendation.title: Fix Normalization And Require Live Proof
recommendation.body: Update peer selection to use canonical iMessage handle normalization, keep or add focused regression coverage, and require redacted after-fix proof showing pairing or replies target the peer chat.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the merged adjacent conversation-repair path and already asked for real behavior proof on this PR.
